**Security: pass-with-notes** at `011933d9f2ac588c8ed4f3ab726a7123e9cd0895`.

The three specific MEDIUM findings from #182 are closed. A separate preexisting holding-instance framing sink remains in the request family; it is not a new #185 authority escalation or an F88 exemption. Current merge state is **DIRTY**: this verdict covers the exact tested tree, not a future merge resolution or readiness.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs | 559-565, 1552-1558, 1623-1638 | Assignment-derived holding instance bypasses initial role-address grammar and enters generated request/check-in/limit text raw | 9/10 |

## Three prior MEDIUMs

| Finding | Result |
|---|---|
| Request IDs in queue wakes/related notices | Closed: queue wake, holder header, check-in, both limit notices, close and withdrawal notices use the message-ID renderer; seat labels use the seat grammar. Correlation keeps the original ID. |
| Model telemetry in large-seat FYIs | Closed: native-status and descriptor fallback converge on the guarded large-seat renderer, with model/role/seat/PA validation including stored values. |
| Output head/notice metadata | Closed: writer, subject, head, result and answers are rendered; kind/role have constrained producers and the displayed path is generated from constrained components. Stored output prose remains untrusted when read. |

## Remaining holding-instance path

An admitted actor able to assign a holding can choose an instance with internal newlines or forged author/instruction framing. Directory admission rejects only slash and leading/trailing whitespace (`crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:1436-1446`).

A canonical send to the broad role can then resolve its sole live holder and replace `request.instance` with that holding's unchecked instance (`delivery/role_send.rs:327-334`). `RoleAddress::display` concatenates those stored fields without rendering/re-parsing. The holder frame interpolates the resulting address before its now-safe request-ID/requester fields. Immediate-send request rows persist the substituted value; check-in, limit, close-address and unsettled-request digest text can subsequently carry it.

Queued drain also substitutes the assignment instance before building the holder header; persistence of that substitution on the queued path was not established. All structured senders remain correct. This is source-established model-facing framing, not a demonstrated malicious model action or direct execution.

Render each role-address component at generated-message sinks, including stored rows and assignment substitutions. Tightening new assignment admission alone would not cover existing data. The passing hostile-stored-instance test proves shell-word quoting while explicitly retaining instance text; it does not prove prompt-framing containment.

## Inventory dispositions

I agree with the explicit **not-blanket-closure** qualification and the three specific closures. The following dispositions need qualification:

| PR-body row | Disagreement or limitation |
|---|---|
| Digest queued address/project: safe by producer | Initial address parsing is not the final invariant: holder resolution substitutes an unchecked holding instance. Unsettled stored rows can render it raw (`pa_watchdog.rs:1300-1317`). Normal project producers are constrained, not arbitrary legacy rows. |
| Request frames/close/withdrawal/limits: fixed for IDs, seats and reasons | Correct for those fields; not complete for assignment-derived addresses, as above. |
| Holding admission gap: future memory/compaction issue | The new holding/memory renderers close those prompt fields, but the same admission gap also feeds current request messages. |
| Background output/event payloads: lines flattened | Completion tails and event text are flattened; inline event **data** is interpolated raw after a size check (`crates/daemon/src/background.rs:1623-1635,1751-1777`). |
| Modal notices: safe producer, registry seat IDs | Classifier labels are closed and pane prose is not exported. Legacy registry IDs are not globally canonical; `stall_body` still uses raw seat display (`crates/core/src/modal_stall.rs:145-154`). No newly introduced path established. |

Other dispositions agree within their stated scope: repository/folder scope remains raw and deferred; current anomaly producers are narrower than arbitrary caller text; cards/notes are capped reported prose in tool responses, not automatic digest content; watchdog ID/model/role and receipt fields are repaired; output body/evidence/link are not in its notice; background and baton/dispatch/decision content remain intentional untrusted prose; holding/memory/compaction labels and usage quota rendering are repaired.

## `fenced()` boundary

`crates/core/src/render.rs:122-133` debug-escapes each complete Unicode scalar inside a generated double-quoted, single-line payload. It cuts before escaping, checks one additional scalar for the truncation marker and always emits its own closing quote. Quotes, backslashes, CR/LF and controls such as ESC/BEL cannot terminate that structural boundary. Production reason callers use the 500-character cap and separately rendered author labels.

The cap bounds input characters, not escaped output bytes. This is **not** a Markdown fence, JSON encoding or a semantic prompt-injection guarantee. Backticks/ordinary markup may remain; a model can still obey quoted instructions. Author attribution preserves untrusted provenance, not permission to execute the reason. Intentional request bodies remain as written under requester framing or returned to their author.

The #175 canonical build/tree renderer and 163/69/238-byte limits remain intact.

## CI and limits

Local and GitHub heads agree; worktree clean. Five checks succeeded, but the branch is currently DIRTY. CI [42462399854](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42462399854) tested synthetic merge `08ac6be554e1c1106dcd8eb422e00f9a41a0adac`, whose tree exactly matches this reviewed head.

JUnit artifact [13610033613](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42462399854/artifacts/13610033613) confirms 2,230 passing cases with no failures/errors, five separately skipped. Executed controls cover render grammars/fencing/watchdog/usage/compaction, forged request-ID queue/header behavior, close-reason containment, output/holding renderers and hostile holder/instance shell-word cases. No hostile native-model delivery canary was run.

Author mutation receipts are not independently certified execution. M6's recorded failure is an ordinary quoted-text assertion; M4 records a failed application before its reported rerun. ddocs reported UNAVAILABLE. New main/conflict resolution requires its own exact-head proof.

No local builds/tests/scripts, hostile reproductions, credentials, product edits or production/delivery/pane/process probes.
